name: HCL Technologies Ltd
title: HCL Technologies Ltd - 532281 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: FY27 guidance of 1% to 4% cc revenue and 17.5% to 18.5% EBIT margin, with two US telecom and SAP-related clients cutting spend; deflation of 2% to 3% for portfolio flagged as an emerging drag.

triggers.label: FY27 revenue guide 1% to 4% cc
triggers.quote: The revenue growth guidance for the full year is 1% to 4% in constant currency and 1.5% to 4.5% for Services.

triggers.label: Two US clients cut discretionary spend
triggers.quote: two large clients in the U.S. during the quarter. We expect the impact to continue for rest of the calendar year as well

triggers.label: AI deflation 2% to 3% on portfolio
triggers.quote: it would translate to 2% to 3% for our portfolio

triggers.label: Software revenue down 28% QoQ
triggers.quote: Our software business declined 28% sequentially, and 14% on a YoY basis.

red_flags.label: Two US clients cutting IT budgets
red_flags.quote: These customers are going through business challenges which are not related specifically to the macroeconomic conditio ns and have decided to scale down their IT budget significantly.

red_flags.label: Q4 software revenue down 28% QoQ
red_flags.quote: Our software business declined 28% sequentially, and 14% on a YoY basis.

red_flags.label: DSO up 3 days to 84
red_flags.quote: Our DSO is currently at 84 days, increased by three days QoQ.

evasions.topic: Deal TCV recovery and product business trajectory
evasions.quote: whether these deals will come back depends on many variables. So it's too early to say and the timing of closure is unpredictable.
I don't want to kind of say that geopolitics is driving this.

summary.headline: HCLTech Q4 FY26 revenue fell 3.3% QoQ to $3,682M with FY27 guidance of 1%-4% cc growth, weighed by two US clients and a soft software quarter.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was $3,682M, down 3.3% QoQ but up 2.4% YoY in constant currency, with services flat QoQ and software down 28.1% QoQ on seasonality and delayed March deal decisions. Operating margin was 16.5% (17.7% ex-restructuring), and net income was $486M at 13.2% of revenue. Management cited cuts in discretionary telecom spend at two large US clients and two discontinued SAP programs, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 1%-4% cc with EBIT margin of 17.5%-18.5%, excluding two pending acquisitions. The company also extended its capital allocation policy for five years, committing to return at least 75% of net income.

financial_highlights.change: 17.7% ex-restructuring (122 bps impact), ~20 bps down YoY
LTM payout INR60; 97.6% of net income

segments.name: IT and Business Services (ITBS)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 0.1% QoQ and 4.3% YoY; FY26 grew 3.7%. Telecom discretionary digital spend cut by two US clients and a retail client's digital platform work affected the segment.

segments.name: Engineering and R&D Services (ERS)
segments.commentary: Q4 fell 1.3% QoQ and grew 3.8% YoY; FY26 grew 9.8%. A manufacturing client with both ER&D and BPO work is among the FY27 headwind clients.

segments.name: Software (HCL Software)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue $307M, down 28.1% QoQ and 14.1% YoY, attributed to seasonality and delayed deal closures. FY26 revenue $1,395M (-4.1%), ARR $1.05B (-0.5%). Management expects FY27 low-single digit, flattish or marginally declining.

segments.name: Advanced AI
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue $155.1M (+6.1% QoQ); annualized FY26 run-rate $620M. Management targets 25%-30% growth in AI-native services; a $100M+ AI Factory deal was won.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance 1%-4% cc; services 1.5%-4.5% cc.

Low end assumes soft discretionary spend and the two US clients ramping down beyond planned ramp-downs; midpoint assumes the two clients land at planned levels; high end assumes moderate discretionary pick-up and a couple of large deals in H1.
Guidance excludes the pending acquisitions of the HPE Telecom Solutions Group carve-out and Jaspersoft; both await US government approval, delayed by a US government shutdown.
Management expects usual Q1 seasonality; mega deal ramp-up is on track and expected to offset the two client headwinds.
Two client-specific challenges in the US are expected to cost about 50 bps of FY27 growth; the telecom impact is expected to persist through calendar 2026.
Capital allocation policy extended for 5 years: at least 75% of net income returned to shareholders.
capex_capacity: AI Factory traction: two major clients now; management hopes to add three or four more in the coming year.
AI Force deployed across 75 distinct accounts; AI Force 2.0 and 2.1 released.
VisionX 2.0 edge AI platform launched, integrating with NVIDIA Metropolis and supporting Dell and HPE hardware.
Hired lateral talent for AI data center infrastructure work; 135,000 employees trained in GenAI, 11,800 AI builders certified.
Management said the benefit of currency depreciation will fund continued investment in sales and GenAI capabilities.
demand_pricing: Q4 bookings were well balanced across service lines, geographies and verticals; large deals included a $100M+ AI Factory deal and a global semiconductor ASIC engineering deal.

Management says a $100M deal now needs roughly 25%-30% more effort to convert, with AI-driven deflation making it about $80M; FY26 TCV held flat at $9.3B, including about $1B of voluntarily walked-away deals.

Management estimates 40% of the industry is AI-disrupted (3%-5% CAGR shrink, translating to 2%-3% for HCLTech's mix), 55% is AI-amplified (about 10%+ growth), and AI-native is about 5% of market growing about 30%.
Europe is softening due to geopolitical escalation; North America is broadly robust apart from the two client issues.
Management said very little AI deflation is visible in reported numbers yet; it expects the effect in FY27 and beyond.

qa_highlights.question: How far could the 3%-5% AI deflation estimate expand over 2-3 years, and which offerings can offset it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said deflation is concentrated in SDLC productivity and could run higher there, but it kept 2%-3% for HCLTech's portfolio, citing limited autonomous production-fix capability. AI Factory is seeing the most traction, with two major clients and three to four more expected.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two SAP programs and two telecom accounts linked, and is there a broader vertical problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the telecom clients and the two other clients (a manufacturing and a retail client, about 50 bps combined) are unrelated with no overlap. The lower end of guidance assumes softness continues; outside these items, business is said to be on the same pace.

qa_highlights.question: Is the telecom impact a full-quarter drag of roughly 1% on growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the SOWs were expected in CY26 spend and were cancelled after dragging, so the impact is more than one month. It assumes the impact lasts through year-end and that it is included in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Are the SAP program cancellations budget-driven or technology-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said they were budget-related: clients de-prioritized modernization, and SAP timeline extensions may be a factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the software/products business?
qa_highlights.answer: Data and operations (IntelliOps, AEX) are growing and will offset declines in the experience portfolio. FY27 expectation is low-single digit, flattish or marginally declining; perpetual license timing is hard to predict, especially government buying.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 software spillover return in Q1, and what is the trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to say whether deals will return, as timing is unpredictable. It noted total revenue growth is 0.5% below services growth, the first such gap in recent years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI-driven pricing deflation already visible, and is it bigger than traditional renewal cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the AI effect is incremental to normal productivity pass-through, very little has played out yet, and it expects the impact from FY27 on, which is why guidance is lower.

risks_watch: Two US clients (telecom and others) cutting discretionary spend; low-end guidance assumes further ramp-downs beyond plan.
Europe softness from geopolitical escalation; management could not give a definitive 12-month view.
Pending acquisitions (HPE Telecom Solutions Group carve-out, Jaspersoft) depend on US government approval; not in guidance.
Software revenue volatility and perpetual license timing, especially government deals.
AI-led deflation may accelerate in FY27 and beyond; management said it is hard to forecast.
DSO rose 3 days QoQ to 84 days; bad debt provision added 19 bps to Q4 margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term AI strategy and capital returns, but cautious and specific about near-term softness: the Q4 miss, the two US client ramp-downs, and FY27 guidance that management says bakes in the low end of demand. It was reluctant to attribute the slowdown to geopolitics or AI deflation, and gave unclear answers on whether software deals will return.
key_quotes: We expect the impact to continue for rest of the calendar year as well, which is accounted for in the guidance we will provide.
It's only prudent to be a little bit more careful about this and spend the energy and organizational bandwidth on more reinventing for the future and enhancing our AI positioning.
We really look forward to growing our AI native services in the 25% to 30% range.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at 1%-4% cc (midpoint 2.5%) with EBIT margin 17.5%-18.5%, excluding pending acquisitions; backing rests on a $9.3B TCV book, a $100M+ AI Factory deal and mega-deal ramp-up, but no specific capacity is added and two US clients are a 50 bps headwind.
